title: Divisors, principal divisors, class group
statement: Let $k$ be algebraically closed and $C$ a smooth connected curve over $k$ ([def-sc-curves]). A *divisor* on $C$ is a finite formal sum $D=\sum_P n_P[P]$ of closed points with integer coefficients; $\operatorname{Div}(C)$ is the free abelian group on those points. For $f\in k(C)^*$ ([def-sc-function-field]), its *principal divisor* is $\operatorname{div}(f)=\sum_Pv_P(f)[P]$, where $v_P$ is the normalized valuation of $\mathcal O_{C,P}$. Its finite support follows from the finite-zero-and-pole theorem for rational functions. The local rings are discrete valuation rings by [lem-sc-smooth-regular] and [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr]. The *divisor class group* is $\operatorname{Cl}(C):=\operatorname{Div}(C)/\operatorname{im}(\operatorname{div})$. For a nonempty open $U\subseteq C$, the associated sub-$\mathcal O_C$-module of the constant sheaf $k(C)$ ([def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]) has sections $\mathcal O_C(D)(U):=\{0\}\cup\{f\in k(C)^*:v_P(f)+n_P\geq0\text{ for every closed }P\in U\}$; over the empty open its section module is zero. The assertion that $\mathcal O_C(D)$ is invertible and that $D\mapsto[\mathcal O_C(D)]$ identifies $\operatorname{Cl}(C)$ with $\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ is a separate theorem. The *degree* is $\deg D:=\sum_Pn_P$. For a disconnected smooth curve, these definitions apply componentwise.
